task: Make Quick Controls and Mode buttons compact square icon-grids on mobile; fix Settings > AI services (and any tab) failing to scroll on narrow viewports

public/styles/controls.css.summary: .modeGrid changed from a single-column list of full-width rows (icon-left/label-right, border-separated) to a compact auto-fit icon grid matching .quickControlsGrid's shape (icon-top/label-bottom, ~44-58px square-ish buttons, sit next to each other). .mode-icon shrunk from 1.5rem to 1.25rem to fit the new square button, .modeGrid .mode-label centered instead of left-aligned.

public/styles/responsive.css.summary: Removed the <=640px override that forced .quickControlsGrid to a single column (grid-template-columns:1fr) -- it now stays the same compact auto-fit multi-column icon grid as wider viewports, matching the Mode grid treatment.

public/styles/settings.css.summary: The <=900px .settingsBody rule now sets align-items:stretch. The desktop align-items:start (so the nav column doesn't stretch to match a taller detail column) had the opposite effect once <=900px turns settingsBody into a two-*row* stack: it stopped .settingsDetail from stretching to fill its minmax(0,1fr) row, so .settingsDetail grew to its content's natural height instead of being height-capped, which meant its own overflow-y:auto never had anything to clip -- any settings tab whose content exceeded the modal's height (AI services, with both providers' key boxes expanded, was the one the owner hit) could not be scrolled to see the rest.

test/public/style.test.js.summary: Updated assertions for the new .modeGrid/.quickControlsGrid compact-grid shape and removed the assertion pinning the old forced single-column mobile override.
